title: Research note: Desargues 10_3 / Pappus 9_3 as T=3 decoder atoms — frame-universal char-2 (CR2) certificates and the one uncertified Pappus frame (conditional on #2162, no κ claim)
body:
**Status: Research note (scoped result, conditional on open PR #2162's Lemma CR2). No κ claim; `certificates/selected-result.json` is untouched.**

This answers OPEN ENDS item 4 of the #2111 handoff ([#1166 comment](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-18932893)) for **Desargues 10_3 and Pappus 9_3 only**: are classical rich configurations tight atoms or counterexamples for (A), cost ≥ v at T = 3? Reye 12_4 and D4 are not covered.

## What was learned

1. **Frame-universal char-2 certificates.** A *frame* uses three configuration points (or three configuration lines) as the coordinate triangle. For every frame, `data/universal.json` stores one char-2 assignment X(point), Y(line). Each assignment respects the frame's supports and has X·Y = 0 exactly on incidences. Coverage: all 221 Desargues frames (GF(16)) and all 151 Pappus frames (GF(4)), plus 1793 certificates for every structured frame of 12 special (extra-triple) Pappus realisations. The verifier checks each one exactly, with no search.
   - **Lemma U** (hand proof in the README): one certificate gives a valid CR2 assignment for **every** decoder configuration built from non-incident (configuration point, configuration line) pairs in that frame, for any v and with repeats allowed. So (A) holds for that whole class, **conditional on CR2**.
   - **Lemma Z:** a frame's zero pattern depends only on the incidences plus any extra collinear or concurrent triples. Desargues has no extra triples (verified: the non-collinearity graph is triangle-free), so the Desargues result covers **every exact realisation over Q**. The Pappus result covers the generic signature and the 12 special signatures that the grid search found (a₂, b₁, b₂ ∈ [−15, 15]).
2. **Side fact (likely classical; not claimed as new).** No exact Desargues 10_3 exists in PG(2,4) or PG(2,8). One parameter fixed, there are 1344 in PG(2,16). Desargues frame certificates therefore need GF(16). On the 740 sampled instances, the per-instance search never needed more than GF(4).
3. **Where the certificate search fails.** I examined 2,166 coordinate systems: every structured frame, plus 13 identity frames that are all of **one mixed type** (e₁ = l∩m, e₃ = A₀, x = 0 the join A₀B₀). Exactly one has no frame-universal certificate over GF(2..16). It is the special Pappus realisation `a=(0,1,-1), b=(0,-15,15)`. In that frame I sampled 2000 decoder configurations (seed 22, v = 6..10):
   - 1912 are CR2-certified.
   - 88 have **no CR2 realisation over GF(2), GF(4) or GF(8)**. This is a bounded search; CR2 allows any char-2 field.
   - 18 of the 88 have f ≤ 26. Their exact minima give **min(cost − v) = 1**, at the instance (v, f, min) = (8, 24, 9).
   - The other 70 (f = 27..45) were skipped and counted.
   - Within this search there is no counterexample and no tight atom without a CR2 realisation. This is a **bounded failed search, not a proof of (A)** for this frame.

## Reproduce

Base commit `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2` (origin/main at submission). From the repository root, using the standard library only:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/three-total-classical-configs/verify.py
```

Expected: every check line (checks 0–8) prints `PASS`, then
`counts {'CR2_certified': 2652, 'noCR2_GF2to8_exact': 18, 'skipped': 70, 'universal_frames': {'desargues': 221, 'pappus': 151}}; min(cost - v) ...: 1`,
then `PASS_THREE_TOTAL_CLASSICAL_CONFIGS`, exit 0. It took about 52 s on CPython 3.14.4. I tested only that version; the syntax is 3.10-compatible.

**Lower-bound scope of the default run.** Default mode re-derives exact minima by pure-Python exhaustion only for the 3 instances with f ≤ 18. For f = 19..26 it checks witness upper bounds, and the lower bounds are recorded enumall output. Check 8 asserts the counts and min(cost − v) = 1. To replay all 18 minima natively, run `gcc -O2 -o /tmp/enumall research/three-total-classical-configs/c/enumall.c` and add `--enumall /tmp/enumall` (PASS; 3–6 min depending on load). That replay re-runs the same vendored C code, so it is not an independent implementation. A local-only pre-submission review re-enumerated all 18 minima with its own C enumerator and found no B with cost < v. Those scripts are not included.

**Controls.**
- `tied_min` and the #2162 six-line atom are classified as having no CR2 realisation over GF(2/4/8). The six-line atom has pure-Python exhaustive minimum 6 = v.
- The stored #2162 GF(4) realisation of `cex_min_1` passes the checker.
- **Seven negative controls** must be rejected: a corrupted certificate entry, a certificate checked against another frame, a GF(4) certificate read over GF(8), a corrupted realisation, a Pappus certificate with two line vectors swapped (incidence-only corruption), a zeroed point, and a constant assignment. The last two are rejected for trivial reasons; the README says so.
- Mutation tests on scratch copies with MANIFEST re-pinned:
  - One flipped certificate bit makes the verifier FAIL.
  - Raising the headline instance's minimum from 9 to 10, with a consistent cost-10 witness, now FAILs check 8 in default mode. Before this revision, only `--enumall` caught it.

Other checks run: `python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/three-total-classical-configs --check-only` → `PASS_PACKAGE_METADATA_AND_PINS`; `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_research_*.py'` → 65 tests OK (2 skipped). `git diff 0fdd7d82 -- upstream certificates` is empty.

## Pins, scope, obligations

- **Vendored, byte-identical, with Apache-2.0 notice in `NOTICE.md`:** `lib/cr2.py`, `c/enumall.c` and four data files from #2162 head `113a718265c62aec301c5695f4bfb9c421bef7ab`, and `enumall.c` from #2111 head `98da76c2839ba38538b510420dec54546ccabf0b`. All are pinned in `MANIFEST.sha256` and `SOURCES.json`.
- **Inherited:** #2162 Lemma CR2 and the a = 0 2-adic corollary (open PR, not re-reviewed here), and the three-total model and cost formula (#2111 §1, from #446/#595).
- **Not formalised:** Lemmas U and Z are short hand proofs. The verifier checks only their finite inputs.
- **Unresolved:**
  - The 70 skipped instances (f = 27..45) in the special frame.
  - Mixed frames of other types, and intersection points of non-configuration lines used as p.
  - Pappus signatures outside the grid, including whether two extra point triples can coexist over Q.
  - Reye 12_4 and D4.
- **`tied_min` control.** The card asked for `tied_min`'s exact minimum 12. Its f = 72 cannot be enumerated, so that value is inherited from #2111/#2162, and the six-line atom serves as the enumerable tight control.
- **Search record:**
  - Frame-universal DFS over GF(2^k), k ≤ 4, with a 2e5 node limit; no timeouts.
  - Special realisations: a Desargues grid of 10584 points, which found 0 signatures (also proved impossible), and a Pappus grid of 27869 points, which found 12 signatures.
  - Samples: 740 structured instances and 2000 special-frame instances, all with seed 22.
  - Stopping rule: f > 26 skipped and counted, stop by 2026-10-15T00:34Z. All requested coverage was completed. "No cost < v" is not an impossibility theorem.
- Open next questions are in the README and `TASK.json`.

## Credit and overlap

- **Predecessors:** DreamingOfClouds #2111 (model, `enumall.c`, `tied_min`, Hesse X2, the OPEN ENDS handoff), #2162 (Lemma CR2, `cr2.py`, the atoms without a CR2 realisation) and #2125; #1590 (Lemma B); #446/#595.
- **Adjacent:** petalas #2193 and RossRichardson #2176.
- **Concurrent:** petalas #2206 certifies `cex_min_1`'s exact cost 21. That is a different question, and this package does not use it.
- **What this adds:** in full-support coordinates the result already follows from CR2 (compare #2111 X2). The new content is the structured, support-restricted frames, the special Pappus realisations, and the one located coordinate system where the certificate search fails.
- **Overlap refresh at submission:** origin/main unchanged since base. No PR or discussion mentions Desargues or Pappus apart from the #1166 handoff and the claim. The #2111/#2162 heads are unchanged.

Sprint: loop 9d24, iteration 2, track 20-39 (complex supplier, decoder sub-line), seed 22. Claim: https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1163#discussioncomment-18936306
